containmentCheck.portable: resolves the policy engine relative to __dirname; accepts an explicit path argument; verified from repo root, from the artifacts directory, and from /tmp

corrections: check_faithfulness.js no longer hard-codes an absolute path; it resolves repo-relative from __dirname, accepts a CLI path, and prints SHA-256 digests of policyEngine.js and policyV1.js.

Ethics text no longer asserts author conduct ('no operational police system was contacted', 'no institutional review was sought'). It now delimits the recorded evaluation and states that real deployment or human-subject work requires applicable institutional and legal review.
Figure 3 relabelled: 2000 ms is a configured timeout reference, 72.69 ms is an observed difference from that reference. Caption and description disclaim component and causal interpretation.
'Dominated by' removed from abstract, results, and conclusion; replaced with non-causal phrasing.
reports/iteration/iter_008_acm_6page_manuscript.md corrected from its stale four-page status.

limitations: No new live-network measurement was taken; all quantitative claims restate dated repository artifacts.

Component-level policy, explanation, endorsement, ordering, and commit timings remain uninstrumented; the 72.69 ms figure is a difference from a configuration constant, not a component timing, and supports no causal claim.
Venue, DOI, and ISBN remain deliberately non-resolvable placeholders; the authordraft watermark is retained until real ACM metadata is supplied.
Two policy rules remain non-subset-safe; this is reported as a finding, not repaired, because changing the engine would invalidate the recorded evaluation.

The eight policy scenarios are fixtures authored with the prototype and were not independently adjudicated.
